check_lei.description: Answer in one step whether an LEI can be relied on today: whether it is a real code at all, who holds it, whether the registration is up to date, and how long until it has to be renewed. A mistyped code is caught before a request is even sent, because the last two characters of an LEI are a checksum over the other eighteen, so a transposed pair is reported as the typo it is rather than as a company that does not exist.

list_changes.description: See what has changed about a company and when, newest first: a new legal name, a moved head office, a renewed registration, a change of owner. Each entry says what the value was and what it became. GLEIF names the field as a path into its XML schema, which is unreadable, so each one is translated into the part of the record it belongs to and the field in plain words. Set a date to see only what changed since then.

description: Look up any company in the world in the official LEI register run by GLEIF, the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation. Search by name to find a company's registered legal name, its official address, the public register it is filed in and the number it is filed under, then follow the ownership up to its parent or down through its subsidiaries. Check whether an LEI is real and still current before trusting it, resolve a BIC, an ISIN or a market code back to the company behind it, list the securities a company has issued, and see what has changed about a record and when. Over two and a half million entities across two hundred countries, published as open data under CC0. No account, no API key, no sign-up.
